name: NIST CSF
description: NIST Cybersecurity Framework v2.0 — technical controls mapped to Identify, Protect, and Detect functions

controls.name: Software is maintained and patched
controls.desc: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk. Security updates close known vulnerabilities promptly.

controls.name: Identity and credential management
controls.desc: No duplicate UID 0 accounts, root SSH disabled, key-based authentication enforced, password policies in place.

controls.name: Remote access hardening
controls.desc: SSH secured with key auth, root login blocked, brute-force limited, X11 forwarding disabled. RDP requires Network Level Authentication.

controls.name: Least privilege enforcement
controls.desc: No extra UID 0, SUID binaries audited, no world-writable system files or directories. UAC enabled and Guest account disabled on Windows.

controls.name: Data-at-rest and in-transit encryption
controls.desc: Strong TLS protocols enforced, weak ciphers disabled, certificates valid, BitLocker active on Windows endpoints.

controls.name: Network filtering and segmentation
controls.desc: Host firewall active, IP forwarding disabled, ICMP redirect and spoofing protections enabled. Legacy SMBv1 and LLMNR disabled.

controls.name: Security configuration baselines
controls.desc: Mandatory access control active, address-space layout randomization on, SUID core dumps disabled, hardened SSH and Windows defaults.

controls.name: Network monitoring
controls.desc: Firewall active for traffic inspection, audit daemon running, time synchronized so log correlation is reliable.

controls.name: Brute-force detection
controls.desc: Failed login count monitored, SSH authentication attempts limited, account lockout configured.

controls.name: Endpoint malware monitoring
controls.desc: Real-time anti-malware protection enabled, signatures fresh, PowerShell script content logged for forensic review.
